translationRepairs: 列傳第十 is the tenth section of the Biographies, not a year.
His grandfather Shao served as Cavalry Commandant.
His grandfather Shao served as Adjutant to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
车骑司马 is the adjutant (sima) on the staff of the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as an ally of Liu Yi; Hun's wife, the Princess of Jinling, was ordered to remarry Prince Lian of Langye.
In the eighth year of Yixi, Hun was executed as an ally of Liu Yi; Hun's wife, the Princess of Jinling, was made to remarry Wang Lian of Langye.
琅邪王練 is Wang Lian of the Langye Wang clan, not a prince named Lian; 改適 means she was made to remarry.
There was a man named Cai Zhizhi; after seeing the Xie An brothers he said to others, "Hongwei's face recalls the Middle Commander, but his character recalls Wenjing."
There was a man named Cai Zhanzhi; after seeing the Xie An brothers he said to others, "Hongwei's face recalls the Middle Commander, but his character recalls Wenjing."
蔡湛之 reads Cai Zhanzhi; 湛 is zhan, not zhi.
His elder brother Yao rose to Imperial Censor and Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Kang of Pengcheng, and died in office.
His elder brother Yao rose to Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk and Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General of Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, and died in office.
御史中丞 is the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk (de facto head of the censorate); the prince's name is Yikang (義康), not Kang.
He rose through the posts to Palace Companion and was further made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
He rose through the posts to Palace Cadet and was further made Palace Attendant.
中庶子 is a Palace Cadet in the heir apparent's household; 侍中 is Palace Attendant.
When Emperor Wen took the throne, Hongwei became Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gates; with Wang Hua, Wang Shoushou, Yin Jingren, and Liu Zhan he was called one of the Five Ministers.
When Emperor Wen took the throne, Hongwei became Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gates; with Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, and Liu Zhan he was called one of the Five Ministers.
黃門侍郎 is Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gates; 王曇首 reads Wang Tanshou.
Hongwei's nephew by marriage, General of the Guards Liu Zhan, said to him, "Public affairs need measured judgment; if you refuse to intervene here, how can you hold office?"
Hongwei's maternal cousin, General of the Guards Liu Zhan, said to him, "Public affairs need measured judgment; if you refuse to intervene here, how can you hold office?"
舅子 here is the son of his maternal uncle, i.e. a maternal cousin, not a nephew by marriage.
He dispatched a thousand men of the Two Guards to finish the burial and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master of Ceremonies.
He dispatched a thousand men of the Two Guards to finish the burial and posthumously conferred on him the office of Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
追贈太常 is a posthumous office (Chamberlain for Ceremonials), not an enfeoffment.
In the twenty-ninth year he was made Palace Companion.
In the twenty-ninth year he was made Palace Cadet of the Heir Apparent.
太子中庶子 is the Palace Cadet of the Heir Apparent.
When the Crown Prince murdered his father and seized the throne, Zhuang was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.
When the Arch-Villain (Liu Shao) murdered his father and seized the throne, Zhuang was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister over the Masses.
元凶 is the historians' epithet Arch-Villain for Liu Shao; 司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works (司空).
When the Emperor ascended the throne, Zhuang was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
When the Emperor ascended the throne, Zhuang was made Palace Attendant.

That year he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing; Zhuang was often ill and did not wish to head selection; he wrote to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, saying, "A pain in both flanks has been with me nearly from birth—it flares once a month, no fewer than two or three times.

That year he was made Minister of Personnel; Zhuang was often ill and did not wish to head selection; he wrote to Grand Marshal Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, saying, "A pain in both flanks has been with me nearly from birth—it flares once a month, no fewer than two or three times.
吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel.
No man in my line has lived long: my great-grandfather died at forty, my grandfather at thirty-three, my father at forty-seven; I myself turn thirty-five this year.
No man in my line has lived long: my great-great-grandfather died at forty, my great-grandfather at thirty-three, my grandfather at forty-seven; I myself turn thirty-five this year.
高祖, 曾祖, 祖 are great-great-grandfather, great-grandfather, and grandfather; the translation shifts each down one generation.
In the fifth year he again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and headed the Forward Army.
In the fifth year he again became Palace Attendant and concurrently served as General of the Van Army.
侍中 is Palace Attendant; 領前軍將軍 means he concurrently held the post of General of the Van Army.
Later at a banquet the Emperor said lightly, "Do you mean to imitate Lord Zhi of Ye?"
Later at a banquet the Emperor said lightly, "Do you mean to imitate Zhi Junzhang?"
郅君章 is Zhi Yun, courtesy name Junzhang, the Han gatekeeper who refused to open the gate at night; there is no 'Ye'.
In the sixth year he again became Minister of the Masters of Writing and headed the National University.
In the sixth year he again became Minister of Personnel and concurrently served as Erudite of the National University.
吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel; 國子博士 is the Erudite of the National University.

Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored Lady Yin died, Zhuang wrote a dirge praising "the track of the Yao Gate," alluding to Zhao Lady, mother of Emperor Zhao of Han, and the Yao Mother Gate; the Deposed Emperor in the Eastern Palace took offense.

Earlier, when Emperor Xiaowu's favored Lady Yin died, Zhuang wrote a dirge praising "the track of the Yao Gate," alluding to Lady Zhao (Zhao Jieyu), mother of Emperor Zhao of Han, and the Yao Mother Gate; the Deposed Emperor in the Eastern Palace took offense.
趙婕妤 is Zhao the Favorite Beauty (jieyu), mother of Emperor Zhao of Han.
Later he became Tutor to the Prince of Xunyang, with additional posts as Director of the Masters of Writing and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
Later he became Tutor to the Prince of Xunyang, with additional posts as Director of the Secretariat and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
中書令 is the Director of the Secretariat (zhongshu), not of the Masters of Writing (shangshu).
At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Xianzi.
At his death he was posthumously granted the office of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, with posthumous title Xianzi.
右光祿大夫 is a posthumous office, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right; there is no purple ribbon and no enfeoffment.
When Emperor Xiaowu toured Guni, he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the imperial train.
When Emperor Xiaowu toured Gushu, he ordered Zhuang to bring Fei in the imperial train.
He was transferred to General of the Left Guard and given the additional title of Attendant Within the Palace.
He was transferred to General of the Left Guard and given the additional title of Supervising Secretary.
給事中 is the Supervising Secretary.
When Fei withdrew after an audience, Can said, "Commander Xie is not dead after all."
When Fei withdrew after an audience, Can said, "Director Xie is not dead after all."
謝令 refers to Fei's late father Xie Zhuang by his office of Director of the Secretariat (中書令), not a military commander.
Emperor Ming of Song once ordered Fei and Xie Feng's son Chao Zong to enter with Feng through Zhuang's gate.
Emperor Ming of Song once ordered Fei and Xie Feng's son Chao Zong to enter through the Fengzhuang Gate.
鳳莊門 is the name of a palace gate (Fengzhuang Gate), not Feng and Zhuang's gate.
Sima Yi served the Wei house all his days and would surely remain a subject to the end.
King Wen of Jin (Sima Zhao) served the Wei house all his days and would surely remain a subject to the end.
晉文 is Sima Zhao, King Wen of Jin, not Sima Yi.
The Emperor was displeased; he brought in Wang Jian as Chief Clerk of the Left and made Fei Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat.
The Emperor was displeased; he brought in Wang Jian as Chief Clerk of the Left and made Fei Palace Attendant and Director of the Palace Library.
侍中 is Palace Attendant; 秘書監 is the Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.
He rose through Minister of Revenue, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Tutor to Prince Xin'an.
He rose through Minister of Justice, Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Tutor to Prince Xin'an.
都官尚書 is the Minister of Justice, not Revenue; 中書令 is the Director of the Secretariat.
His brother Yue was then Minister of the Masters of Writing; reaching the commandery Fei sent Yue several hu of wine with a note: "Drink hard and stay out of affairs."
His brother Yue was then Minister of Personnel; reaching the commandery Fei sent Yue several hu of wine with a note: "Drink hard and stay out of affairs."
吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel.
In Jianwu four he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; he refused.
In Jianwu four he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Secretariat; he refused.
中書令 is the Director of the Secretariat.
When Jiankang was pacified, Fei and Yin were summoned as Army Advisers and Sacrificial Officers; neither came.
When Jiankang was pacified, Fei and Yin were summoned as Libationers of Army Consultation; neither came.
軍諮祭酒 is a single office, Libationer of Army Consultation.

At his accession edicts summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Left of the Purple Ribbon, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Yin as Regular Attendant, Special Advance, and Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon; again both refused.

At his accession edicts summoned Fei as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Yin as Regular Attendant, Specially Advanced, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right; again both refused.
左/右光祿大夫 are Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness of the Left/Right; no purple ribbon is involved; 特進 is the honorific Specially Advanced.

Then General of the Guards Sima Wang Guo was sent to persuade Fei; Fei consulted He Yin; Yin, wishing to stand alone in integrity, deceived him: "In an age of rising kings, how can one stay apart forever?"

Then Wang Guo, Adjutant to the General Commanding the Army was sent to persuade Fei; Fei consulted He Yin; Yin, wishing to stand alone in integrity, deceived him: "In an age of rising kings, how can one stay apart forever?"
領軍司馬 is the adjutant (sima) of the General Commanding the Army; Sima is a title here, not part of the name.
An edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
An edict made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister over the Masses, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses, not the Minister of Works.
In the fifth year he was reassigned as Director of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and Guard General, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
In the fifth year he was reassigned as Supervisor of the Secretariat, Minister over the Masses, and Guard General, but he firmly declined and did not accept.
中書監 is the Supervisor of the Secretariat, senior to the Director (中書令).
His son Xuan rose to Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister of Works and was dismissed for slaughtering an ox.
His son Xuan rose to Chief Clerk of the Right of the Minister over the Masses and was dismissed for slaughtering an ox.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses.
He rose to Grand Master of the Right of the Purple Ribbon.
He rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right.
右光祿大夫 is the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right; no purple ribbon.
Under Chen he held Minister of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Masters of Writing, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works.
Under Chen he held Minister of Personnel, Director of the Secretariat, Palace Attendant, and Chief Clerk of the Left of the Minister over the Masses.
吏部尚書 Minister of Personnel; 中書令 Director of the Secretariat; 侍中 Palace Attendant; 司徒 Minister over the Masses.
He rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was known for plain elegance.
He rose to Gentleman of the Board of Personnel and was known for plain elegance.
吏部郎 is a Gentleman of the Board of Personnel.
He died as Chief Clerk to the General of the North.
He died as Chief Clerk to the General of the Gentlemen of the North Household.
北中郎 is the General of the Gentlemen of the North Household (北中郎將).
He was quick and resourceful; once drinking with Liu Jiao, after long deferral Jiao said, "Xie Zhuang's son cannot be called unable to drink."
He was quick and resourceful; once drinking with Liu Quan, after long deferral Quan said, "Xie Zhuang's son cannot be called unable to drink."
悛 is read Quan; the name is Liu Quan.
Jiao was deeply ashamed and fell silent.
Quan was deeply ashamed and fell silent.
Later he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
Later he was made Minister of Personnel.
吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel.
When Yan first received the gilded sword, Yue told him, "Your house produced a Grand Tutor and got only six guards—why suddenly twenty for one affair?"
When Yan first received the gilded sword, Yue told him, "My own family's Grand Tutor received only six sword-bearers—why suddenly twenty for one affair?"
身家太傅 refers to Yue's own family (the Grand Tutor Xie An), not Wang Yan's; 班劍 are ceremonial sword-bearing guards.
He was additionally made General of the Right.
He was additionally made General of the Right Army.
右軍將軍 is the General of the Right Army.
In Yongtai one he died as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Jianzi.
In Yongtai one he died as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent; he was posthumously granted the office of Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous title Jianzi.
贈 confers a posthumous office, not an enfeoffment.
When Fei was in Wuxing, Yue saw him off at Zhengliu Isle; Fei pointed at Yue's mouth and said, "Here one should only drink wine."
When Fei was in Wuxing, Yue saw him off at Zhenglu Isle; Fei pointed at Yue's mouth and said, "Here one should only drink wine."
In Tianjian one he was Gentleman of the Secretariat, managing the Masters of Writing; soon he received full appointment.
In Tianjian one he was Gentleman of the Secretariat, managing the affairs of the Board of Personnel; soon he received full appointment.
掌吏部事 is managing the Board of Personnel.
Once while attending he was ordered with Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Xie to compose answering poems; the wording was superb, and when told to rewrite it he again hit the mark.
Once while attending he was ordered with Palace Attendant Wang Jian to compose answering poems; the wording was superb, and when told to rewrite it he again hit the mark.
王暕 is Wang Jian (暕 jiǎn); 侍中 is Palace Attendant.
As Attendant-in-Ordinary he greatly enjoyed wine; at a banquet he traded insults with Regular Attendant Xiao Chen and was reported by the relevant office.
As Palace Attendant he greatly enjoyed wine; at a banquet he traded insults with Regular Attendant Xiao Chen and was reported by the relevant office.
Later he was made Minister of the Masters of Writing and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
Later he was made Minister of Personnel and sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel.
Palace Aide Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and brothers were domineering; previous administrators all bowed to them.
Secretariat Drafter Huang Muzhi's family lived in Wucheng; his sons and brothers were domineering; previous administrators all bowed to them.
中書舍人 is a Secretariat Drafter.
He died in office and was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Masters of Writing.
He died in office and was posthumously granted the office of Director of the Secretariat.
贈中書令 is a posthumous office, Director of the Secretariat.
He was Household Steward to the Heir Apparent and headed the secretariat; Crown Prince Zhaoming deeply favored and received him.
He was Household Steward to the Heir Apparent and was in charge of records; Crown Prince Zhaoming deeply favored and received him.
掌管記 is charge of records and correspondence, not a secretariat.
Director Ren Fang went out as Administrator of Xin'an; Ju wrote in parting, "How can one remember the sighing elder—yet you deeply trust this old man's charge."
Director Ren Fang went out as Administrator of Xin'an; he wrote a parting poem to Ju, "How can one remember the sighing elder—yet you deeply trust this old man's charge."
別舉詩 is Ren Fang's farewell poem to Ju, not Ju's poem.
He rose to Minister of the Left Household and was transferred to head the Masters of Writing.
He rose to Minister of the Left Household and was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
掌吏部尚書 is the Minister of Personnel.
He was additionally made Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing.
He was additionally made Palace Attendant and transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
侍中 is Palace Attendant; 尚書右僕射 is the Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and General Who Assists the Left.
He entered as Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and General Who Assists the Left.
Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Attendant-in-Ordinary and General unchanged.
Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; Palace Attendant and General unchanged.

The Emperor said, "Ju not only held many offices—he was also a model of human conduct, long famed in public expectation; I regret not having conferred more; posthumously enfeoff him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies."

The Emperor said, "Ju not only held many offices—he was also a model of human conduct, long famed in public expectation; I regret not having conferred more; posthumously grant him the offices of Palace Attendant, General of the Central Guard, and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies."
贈 confers posthumous offices, not an enfeoffment; 侍中 is Palace Attendant.
Under Liang he served as Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Jian'an.
Under Liang he served as Palace Cadet of the Heir Apparent and Administrator of Jian'an.
太子中庶子 is the Palace Cadet of the Heir Apparent.
He rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Minister of Justice.
He rose to Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, and Minister of Justice.
侍中 is Palace Attendant; 中書令 is the Director of the Secretariat.
His son Yan held Attendant-in-Ordinary, Imperial Censor, and Grand Master of Ceremonies;
His son Yan held Palace Attendant, Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk, and Grand Master of Ceremonies;
侍中 is Palace Attendant; 御史中丞 is the Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
His father Xuan Da served Liang as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
His father Xuan Da served Liang as Palace Attendant.
